Main computation पूरा (script: /workspace/analysis.py, log: /workspace/out/analysis_output.txt; सभी comma-decimal strings numeric convert कें गए; inference केवल 5 raw 100-yr bins पर, interpolation का use सिर्फ़ robustness note तक)।

═══ 1) WINDOW LEVELS + TRENDS (3400–3000 BCE, all 5 bins = "MN") ═══
Levels (raw Z, capital.csv):
          MonumentCount  AxesCelts  HatchetSword  Dagger  HouseSize
3400 BCE        -0.465       0.37        -0.43    -0.58       2.05

3000 BCE        -0.363       0.80        -0.43    -0.58       0.19

series        start    end    ΔZ     slope/century (stderr)  ols_p   dir
MonumentCount -0.465 -0.363 +0.102   +0.069 (0.205)          0.759   rising
AxesCelts      0.370  0.800 +0.430   +0.134 (0.333)          0.714   rising
HatchetSword  -0.430 -0.430  0.000   +0.001 (0.002)          0.559   flat
Dagger        -0.580 -0.580  0.000   0.000 (zero variance)     —     flat
HouseSize      2.050  0.190 -1.860   -0.457 (0.138)          0.046   falling
RANK ORDER OF TOTAL CHANGE: AxesCelts +0.43 > MonumentCount +0.10 > HatchetSword 0.00 = Dagger 0.00 > HouseSize −1.86.
Both MonumentCount and AxesCelts are hump-shaped with a common PEAK at 3200 BCE (+0.91 and +2.60). Diagnostic context: HatchetSword −0.43 and Dagger −0.58 are pinned at the FLOOR of their entire 39-bin record (full ranges −0.44…2.95 and −0.58…3.33); HouseSize 3400 BCE = 2.05 is the MAXIMUM of the whole record.

═══ 2) DESCRIPTIVE CORRELATIONS (n=5, df=3 — supporting only) ═══
focal / symbolic      pearson r (p)   95% CI          spearman ρ (p)   |r| needed for p<.05
MC / HatchetSword      +0.285 (0.642)  −0.798…+0.933   +0.354 (0.559)   0.878
MC / Dagger            UNDEFINED (zero variance) → levels only: mean|MC−Dagger| = 0.641
MC / HouseSize         −0.352 (0.562)  −0.942…+0.769   −0.410 (0.493)   0.878
AC / HatchetSword      −0.106 (0.865)  −0.904…+0.856   +0.181 (0.770)   0.878
AC / Dagger            UNDEFINED (zero variance) → mean|AC−Dagger| = 1.558
AC / HouseSize         −0.166 (0.789)  −0.914…+0.839   −0.368 (0.542)   0.878
Fragility: every CI straddles zero and would need |r|≥0.878 to be significant; no inferential claim is made. Supplementary: MonumentCount vs AxesCelts r=0.868 (p=0.057, CI −0.06…0.99), ρ=0.616 — the strongest covariation in the window is between the two focal series themselves, not with symbolic capital.

═══ 3) CO-MOVEMENT (PRIMARY EVIDENCE) ═══
Bin-to-bin Δ:
              MC     AC    HS    Dagger  HouseSize
3400→3300   +0.332  -0.05  0.00   0.00    -1.26
3300→3200   +1.046  +2.28  0.00   0.00     0.00
3200→3100   -0.561  -1.80  +0.01  0.00    -0.85
3100→3000   -0.714   0.00  -0.01  0.00    +0.25
Sign agreement (usable transitions): MC–HouseSize 1/3 (33%, corr-of-changes −0.799); AC–HouseSize 2/2 (100%, only 2 usable); MC–HatchetSword 1/2; AC–HatchetSword 0/1; Dagger 0/4 (never moves) → co-movement with symbolic capital is inconsistent/absent, and the only two series that move together are MonumentCount and AxesCelts (2/3).

═══ 4) POLLEN OPENNESS SIDEBAR (exploratory, NOT in hypothesis) ═══
Belau-only proxy (time_series series): pollen_inter +1.645 (3400 BCE) → −1.157 (3000 BCE), Δ −2.80, slope −0.77/century (annual interp, only 21 raw pollen points in window); pollen_inter_100 slope −0.72/century. Two-site option: MEAN +0.078 → −1.856 (−0.63/century), SMOOTH_MEAN_100y −0.59/century — same direction, different levels. Exploratory r vs focal (n=5): MC −0.017/+0.144, AC −0.215/−0.081 (ρ up to −0.667, p=0.219) → no usable coupling. ASSUMPTION (not fact): PC1 high = more landscape clearance.

═══ 5) ROBUSTNESS (labelled; headline unchanged) ═══
3500–2800 BCE (n=8): MC +0.55 rising, AC +0.82 rising, HouseSize −2.16 falling (ols_p=0.010), HatchetSword flat, Dagger constant → same sign pattern. all-MN bins = exactly 3400…3000 BCE, so identical to window by construction. Annual-interpolated slopes (descriptive, NOT independent): MC +0.106, AC +0.157, HatchetSword +0.002, Dagger 0.000, HouseSize −0.450 per century — same directions as the 5-bin slopes.

═══ FINAL HYPOTHESIS (answer to the question) ═══
Between 3400 and 3000 BCE the number of monuments and the axes/celts record both increase relative to their own long-term baseline, but they do so WITHOUT — and partly against — the elements of symbolic capital. MonumentCount rises by +0.10 Z (−0.47 → −0.36, peaking at +0.91 in 3200 BCE) and AxesCelts by +0.43 Z (+0.37 → +0.80, peaking at +2.60 in 3200 BCE), the two tracking each other (descriptive r = 0.87); these are the largest positive changes of any series in the window. In the same 400 years the symbolic-capital elements do not rise at all: Hatchets&Swords stay pinned at the floor of their entire record (≈ −0.43 Z, ΔZ = 0.00) and Daggers are literally constant at their record minimum (−0.58 Z, zero variance, so no correlation is computable), while House Size falls steeply (ΔZ = −1.86, ≈ −0.46 Z/century) from the highest value in the whole dataset (2.05 Z) down to near-average — a decline from an exceptional early-window maximum rather than a collapse below baseline. Accordingly we hypothesise that monumental construction and axe deposition were driven by a communal/dedicatory (non-prestige-goods) dynamic that was decoupled from symbolic-capital display: as monuments and axes peaked around 3200 BCE, house size, daggers and hatchets/swords were static or contracting, and descriptive associations are uniformly weak (all |r| ≤ 0.36 with CIs spanning about −0.95…+0.93; bin-to-bin sign agreement with House Size only 1/3 for monuments and 2/2 for axes). Conversely, the decline of monuments and axes after the 3200 BCE peak cannot be attributed to symbolic capital, which never varied in this window. Caveats retained in the wording: (i) House Size is a proxy for household/domestic as well as symbolic capital, so its decline may reflect economic re-organisation; (ii) all statistics rest on 5 independent 100-year bins, so direction, magnitude and rank order — not p-values — carry the argument; (iii) the data contain no absolute counts, so every magnitude is expressed in Z (standardised) units.

Workflow: load capital.csv (comma→dot decimal parsing, BCE→CE = −BCE) as canonical 100-yr raw Z table (verified bit-identical to time_series raw columns) → slice 3400–3000 BCE (5 bins) → levels, ΔZ, OLS slope/century, direction class (|ΔZ|<0.1 = flat) → Pearson r + Fisher-z 95% CI + Spearman ρ with explicit n=5 fragility threshold, Dagger skipped for zero variance → bin-to-bin Δ sign-agreement and rank-order of change as primary evidence → focal-focal and non-symbolic context checks → Belau pollen sidebar (interpolated, plus two-site MEAN option) → labelled wider-window (3500–2800 BCE, all-MN) and annual-interpolated robustness, with no pseudo-replicated inference.

payload.hypothesis: Between 3400 and 3000 BCE monuments and axes increase together while elements of symbolic capital do not: MonumentCount rises +0.10 Z (-0.47 -> -0.36, peaking at +0.91 in 3200 BCE) and AxesCelts +0.43 Z (+0.37 -> +0.80, peaking at +2.60 in 3200 BCE), the two tracking each other (descriptive r = 0.87), whereas Hatchets&Swords stay pinned at the floor of their record (~-0.43 Z, dZ 0.00), Daggers are constant at their record minimum (-0.58 Z, zero variance) and House Size falls steeply (dZ -1.86, ~-0.46 Z/century) from the highest value in the whole dataset (2.05 Z) to near average. We therefore hypothesise that monumental construction and axe deposition after 3400 BCE were driven by a communal/dedicatory dynamic decoupled from prestige-goods and household symbolic display: monuments and axes peaked around 3200 BCE precisely while house size, daggers and hatchets/swords were static or contracting, associations are uniformly weak (all |r| <= 0.36, CIs about -0.95..+0.93; bin-to-bin sign agreement with House Size 1/3 for monuments, 2/2 for axes), and the post-3200 BCE decline of monuments and axes cannot be attributed to symbolic capital, which never varied in this window. Caveats: House Size is also an economic/domestic proxy; all statistics rest on 5 independent 100-year bins so direction, magnitude and rank order carry the argument; magnitudes are Z-standardised because the data contain no absolute counts.
payload.workflow: 1) Parse capital.csv with comma->decimal conversion, convert BCE to signed CE (CE = -BCE); verified identical (max abs diff 0.0) to time_series_data.csv raw Z columns, so it is used as the canonical 100-year raw-Z table. 2) Slice 3400-3000 BCE inclusive = 5 bins (all period MN). 3) Per series report levels, dZ 3400->3000, OLS slope per century with stderr, direction class (|dZ|<0.1 flat), up/down steps, unique counts, and rank order of change. 4) Descriptive Pearson r with Fisher-z 95% CI plus Spearman rho for MonumentCount/AxesCelts vs each symbolic element, printing the |r| needed for p<0.05 at n=5; Dagger skipped (zero variance) and described by levels. 5) PRIMARY co-movement evidence: bin-to-bin change-sign agreement, corr of changes, rank order of total change, plus focal-focal (MonumentCount vs AxesCelts) and non-symbolic context series. 6) Pollen openness sidebar from Belau-only pollen_inter / pollen_inter_100 (annual, interpolated) with two-site MEAN/SMOOTH_MEAN_100y shown as an option; flagged exploratory and excluded from the hypothesis. 7) Labelled robustness: 3500-2800 BCE (n=8), all-MN (equals the window), and annual-interpolated slopes reported as descriptive only to avoid pseudo-replication. 8) Tables exported to out/results.xlsx and CSVs; full stdout in out/analysis_output.txt.
payload.primary_evidence: trend direction/magnitude, rank order of change and bin-to-bin sign agreement
payload.supporting_evidence: Pearson r + Spearman rho on n=5 bins with CIs and fragility note
payload.artifacts_note: analysis.py is the executed analysis; out/ holds printed diagnostics and result tables
